author.name: Thomas Szasz
author.heading: About Thomas Szasz
author.bio: Thomas Szasz taught psychiatry at the State University of New York Upstate Medical University and opposed involuntary psychiatric interventions. Alongside his longer arguments about psychiatric authority, he published compact definitions and aphorisms designed to expose evasive uses of language.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The joke turns the familiar moral warning against retaliation into a description of rationalization. Its second half explains why invoking another person’s wrongdoing can still be attractive even when it provides no ethical justification.

Szasz’s collection consists of similarly compressed observations about language, responsibility and authority. The specific page reference is useful for locating the line, but the uninspected original page remains a limit on this check.
